meta.definition: Editorial assessment of the named AI-compatible CMS workflow, not a ranking of CMS quality.

statusDefinition.Production: Dependable enough for a controlled recurring workflow today.
statusDefinition.Test: Worth piloting, but access, maturity or control needs a bounded test.
statusDefinition.Research: Useful specialist capability, not a daily operating interface.

positives: Draft creation and post-section editing are documented.
Existing WordPress roles and tool controls govern access.
negatives: Tool availability varies by site, plan and account settings.
Shared account-level settings need review before enabling writes.

positives: Uses a common WordPress Abilities contract.
The site can define narrowly scoped operations and permission checks.
negatives: Requires technical setup and suitable Abilities.
Editorial coverage varies by plugin and site configuration.

positives: Combines structured content and site-design operations.
Uses existing site permissions and roles.
negatives: New localised CMS items are not supported through this route.
Some visual operations require the Designer, and new site creation stays in the dashboard.

positives: Explicit entry and release publication tools.
Per-environment tool gating supplements user permissions.
negatives: Each environment needs MCP app configuration.
Local-server defaults do not restrict a PAT to one environment.

positives: Schema-aware document operations and explicit publishing tools.
Supports draft and release-version workflows.
negatives: Localisation depends on project schema and conventions.
Wrong draft or release IDs can target a different editorial state.

positives: Reuses existing Directus permissions.
Content operations do not require a separate middleware layer.
negatives: Publication and localisation need project-specific modelling.
A broad service role can expose more data than an editorial assistant needs.

positives: Documented article and page creation with publication settings.
Explicit API scopes provide a configurable access boundary.
negatives: Requires an app and custom integration work.
Editing, deletion and localisation are not verified by the creation endpoints assessed here.

positives: Official product operations use WordPress permission checks.
The adapter can expose supported store tasks directly to an assistant.
negatives: The integration remains developer preview.
Version changes, extension fields and publication behaviour need a store-level test.

positives: Documented page and blog operations cover recurring content edits.
Blog publication is explicit in the API.
negatives: Requires a custom authenticated integration.
Page visibility and blog publication have different semantics.

positives: Explicit CMS page and block operations.
CMS access is controlled through integration permissions.
negatives: Requires custom engineering and deployment-specific checks.
An API write does not prove the storefront or Page Builder layout is correct.
